chapter: Double bass drums and the great drummers
title: First meeting Buddy Rich
summary: He met Rich in Cedar Rapids while still in school, found him brisk, and became friends after asking about the radio microphones.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: When’s the first time you met Buddy Rich? Do you remember meeting him for the first time?

I met him in Cedar Rapids, Iowa. He was with Tommy Dorsey’s band. I was still going to high school at that time. He impressed me very much. I heard him on radio broadcasts coming from the Hotel Astor in New York with Tommy Dorsey’s band. I said, I’ve got to meet that guy, because it sounds like he’s got a lot of technique – not only technique, but he plays good with the band. From that point on, I joined Benny’s band, and we got to know one another. That relationship went on for about – right up to when he died.
What was he like when you first met him? Because he has a reputation for being abrasive.
He was brisk, yeah. That’s a good title for him, brisk. But he took a liking to me, because I was asking the right questions.
On your radio broadcast from New York, how did they set up the microphones? Because I could tell all the beats that you were playing.” He said, “The heck with the microphones. That came from me.”

From that point on, we chatted for a while. I got his address – New York address. I called him. We got to be good friends from that point on, close friends. We had a lot of high respect for one another. We played together quite a few times too.
